independent_optimization.selected_instruction:
Rewrite task strategy for procedures_devices with strict source fidelity and clinical completeness. Extract only explicitly documented procedures, devices and nonpharmacologic therapies for the index patient. Never attribute procedures, devices or timing from abstract, discussion, figure captions, tables with mixed case columns, or other patients, literature-review cases, cohort averages, specimen reagents or general recommendations to the index patient. Keep patient identity boundaries; do not transfer procedures between mother, fetus, newborn, multiple cases or mixed-case table rows.

Distinguish real execution status: completed vs ordered/planned/declined/cancelled/device_present/removed/historical. Completed surgery/biopsy/intubation differs from an order, recommendation, declined intervention or cancelled procedure. 'Scheduled for nephrectomy' is planned, not completed. 'Status post nephrectomy' is historical completed. Do not infer a procedure from scar, medication, expected standard of care, or from imaging findings unless the source explicitly identifies the procedure performed on this patient.

Include surgery, diagnostic invasive procedures, dialysis, mechanical ventilation support, rehabilitation, radiotherapy procedures, and devices such as pacemakers, catheters, prostheses, assistive devices when documented. Preserve distinction between implant/device and the procedure that placed or removed it using separate items when needed. Record body_site, laterality, indication, finding and complication only when stated; do not invent.

Keep event timing, negation, uncertainty and cancellation. Do not infer laterality from another lesion or silently combine multiple operations. Evidence must contain verbs such as underwent, performed, initiated, started, stopped, removed, extubated, extubated, discontinued, completed, remained in place that support the action and subject separately from the procedure name.

Evidence requirements: For each ProcedureDevice item provide at least one Evidence with exact contiguous source text including qualifiers and negation. Use the displayed segment ID as source_section. The exact quote must occur within that segment. Quote table headers and time headings separately when needed; never synthesize a quote joining nonadjacent rows or nonadjacent segments. source_section may be a heading actually present in the source or null only if no heading exists; do not leave source_section null when a segment ID is available. Do not copy target labels or another source format as evidence.

TimeMention: use verbatim temporal expression. Never invent dates or durations. date_iso is YYYY-MM-DD only if explicitly present as an unshifted full date; otherwise null. relation and anchor must reflect explicit anchors such as admission, surgery, etc., not publication date.

Output fields are mandatory. All keys required; use null/unknown for unstated values. Do not skip difficult fields to pass validation. Empty items array is valid when no supported facts exist. Coverage means task reviewed supplied source, not that patient history is complete. documentation_status = documented includes positive, negative, possible and historical facts; silence is not_documented, never a clinical negative. documentation_evidence is for explicitly_unknown/not_applicable only; fact evidence stays on each item.

Negative controls: Explicit negative 'No prior surgery' is one scoped absent history item with name preserving that phrase; do not enumerate unperformed operations. 'Biopsy declined' is affirmed declined procedure, not absent tumor or completed biopsy. Missing mention means empty items, not no surgical history or no implanted device. An example in instructions is not patient evidence. Populate only claims supported by supplied record.

Rewrite observations extraction to enforce complete, source-faithful recall with strict patient identity and temporal binding. Preserve the immutable schema and never instruct skipping difficult fields, facts or evidence to pass validation.

Scope and fidelity
- Extract only measurements and test findings: laboratories, vitals, imaging, pathology, microbiology, physiologic and other tests. Preserve exact test name, value, comparator < <= > >= =, unit, specimen, method, site, reference interval and time when reported.
- Do not drop normal quantitative laboratory values. Do not invent a result from "labs were normal". Record a relevant qualitative finding when explicitly stated.
- Do not infer abnormality from external reference ranges. Flag=high/low/normal requires wording or an explicit source-provided interval supporting the classification. Leave flag=unknown otherwise.
- Test status and result polarity are separate. Example: 'HIV test negative' is assertion=present, status=resulted, flag=negative. 'No HIV test was performed' is status=not_performed. Ordered tests are status=ordered, not a negative result.
- Treatment goals, titration targets and desired therapeutic ranges are NOT measured test results. Do not create an observation for the target alone or mark it resulted.

Completeness and uncertainty
- Retain all actual measured findings and explicitly documented performed tests, including repeated findings at distinct times. Keep repeated values at different times as separate items. Never average, select the most abnormal, convert units, infer eGFR/creatinine clearance, calculate scores, or use publication date as sample date.
- Preserve '<0.01' and other qualifiers rather than replacing with zero. Use text_value when a number or range cannot be safely represented. Distinguish absolute vs percentage counts, plasma/serum/urine specimens, and oxygen settings during a blood gas when written.
- For a named test with an unstated result use result_absent_reason=not_reported, not inferred normality. Pending has status=pending, result_absent_reason=pending, text_value=null, numeric_value=null. Missing mention produces no item.

Tables and time binding
- For measurements in a table, preserve the time from the row-group heading, e.g., On admission versus At 48 h, not merely a general table caption.
- Include an additional exact quotation of that heading from the SAME table-row segment in the item's evidence so time.text occurs literally in its evidence. Keep the exact data-row quotation as well.
- Do not concatenate noncontiguous excerpts into a fabricated quotation. Do not erase a documented time to satisfy validation. Keep each patient's column and each time point distinct. Evidence must bind the value to the correct test and patient, not merely match the number somewhere in the record.
- For narrative findings, add a separate exact time quotation from that patient's corresponding event when needed.

Naming and clinical precision
- Preserve specimen for ABG as arterial blood when the source describes arterial blood gas parameters. Preserve specimen, value/unit, planned vs performed status, and separate encounters.
- Split named laboratory/immunohistochemical panel members into individual observations. Distinguish performed test from absent finding.
- For observations split numeric magnitude, comparator and unit into their fields. Preserve exact result notation in text_value including scientific exponents; keep reference intervals separate.
- Accept name variants that the source uses, e.g., Ca2+ / Calcium ionized, CRP / C.reactive, WBC / white blood cell count, Hemoglobin / Haemoglobin. Name must be derived from source wording, not normalized to a canonical term.

Evidence and documentation
- Each Observation requires evidence with quote exactly contiguous from source and source_section. Quote table headers and time headings separately when needed. Only supplied source text supports facts, not target labels or another source format.
- Root coverage = complete means this task reviewed the supplied source. Document limitations about mixed case columns, shared time headings, or narrative-only reporting. documentation_status reflects presence of documented facts.
- Empty output is valid when no supported facts exist. Never memorize cases, source IDs or answer values. Patient identity is preserved by binding evidence to the correct case column and time heading.

Rewrite the timeline_v2 extraction strategy to eliminate clinical omissions and contradictions while preserving schema, source fidelity, patient identity, uncertainty and completeness. Never instruct skipping difficult fields or facts to pass validation, and do not memorize cases, source IDs or answer values.

Task constraints to preserve:
* Return patient-timeline/2 JSON only for the specified record_id and patient. Describe only this patient. Never invent encounters or dates.
* Schema is immutable: LongitudinalEvent requires event_id, record_id, episode_id, kind in [presentation,history,diagnosis,test,treatment,adverse_event,outcome,follow_up,plan,other], occurrence in [occurred,planned,conditional,unknown], description, fact_ids array, evidence array, attribution_evidence array, times array. TemporalEdge requires edge_id, from_event_id, to_event_id, relation in [before,after,same_time,during,overlaps], offset or null, evidence establishing the pair and relation.
* Every evidence and attribution span must supply only a known segment_id and an exact unique quote. Code derives source_id, segment_sha256 and Unicode positions; do not calculate or invent those fields.
* Use fact_ids only from known_fact_ids for this record; empty array is allowed. The registry associates IDs with unreviewed extracted values: verify every event and link against primary source, not registry alone. Link events to corresponding extracted fact_ids whenever the source supports that association.
* Times must preserve literal precision. Use TimeExpression with text, kind in [calendar,relative,duration,age,gestational_age,postnatal_age,order_only], precision, calendar_value only literal YYYY/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD, and evidence. Keep month/year offsets in their own units. Times may be [] for unknown time.
* Include unknown-time events, failed treatments, follow-up and plans, keeping occurred, planned, conditional and unknown distinct.

Clinical completeness and fidelity steps:
1. Diagnose omissions from feedback: explicitly check for presentation, history, investigations, treatment initiation, treatment response / lack of response / failure, adverse events, complications, deterioration, outcome including death/discharge, and planned follow-up. For ethylene glycol intoxication cases ensure thrombolysis treatment, post-thrombolysis neurological non-improvement, acute deterioration with time anchor, intubation/mechanical ventilation, hemodynamic instability, laboratory acidosis, diagnostic toxicology, ICU transfer, specific complications such as pneumonia, acute kidney injury, anuria, creatinine peak, and death or discharge with day offsets are represented as separate events when documented.
2. Preserve uncertainty and contradictions: if source states unknown status, conflicting values or unreviewed registry items, represent occurrence as unknown and keep the conflicting descriptions with separate evidence. Do not resolve contradictions by omission.
3. Relative clinical sequence over dates: distinguish past history, presentation, investigations, treatment, adverse events or failed response, treatment changes, discharge and follow-up when documented. Order the clinical occurrence, not when it was narrated. A history reported at admission describes an earlier event.
4. Temporal edges: create before/after edges with offset=null when source establishes order without a duration. Edges must cite evidence for BOTH events and their relation, not just a time word. Do not derive chronology from paragraph order. Preserve simultaneity only when stated; leave incomparable events unordered.
5. Kind discipline: use only allowed kinds. Do not use invented kinds such as symptoms_function. Map clinical findings to presentation, history, test, treatment, adverse_event, outcome, plan, other as appropriate.
6. Source verification: for each candidate event from the registry, locate primary source quote confirming the event, its occurrence status and any time expression. If verification fails, do not create the event from registry alone.
7. No field erasure to pass validation: keep all required fields populated. If a field is genuinely unknown, use empty array for fact_ids/times or occurrence=unknown, not omission.
8. Limitations: record limitations for missing temporal anchors, ambiguous ordering, or registry-source mismatches.

Apply this strategy consistently to timeline_v2 extractions, ensuring clinical steps are present, temporally linked with source-cited edges, and uncertainty is preserved.

For coverage_repair tasks, treat the supplied CURRENT extraction as the immutable baseline and repair it only by source-verified evidence. Do not change immutable schema contracts, patient identity, validator-required fields, or previously accepted fact values. Preserve every previously accepted fact and value exactly as documented, including subject, assertion, temporality, time with text/relation/anchor/date_iso verbatim, evidence array with exact contiguous quotes and source_section, name, kind, action, body_site, laterality, indication, finding, complication, and for observations when present: result_absent_reason, name, kind, status, text_value, numeric_value, comparator, unit, flag, reference_range_text, specimen, method, body_site.

Diagnose clinical omissions and contradictions from feedback against the original patient source for the target article_id/patient_id/record_id/stage. Re-read the source and locate each hypothesis claim in the source text; add a missing item only when a direct source quote independently supports the claim. Never copy audit hypotheses or feedback claims without explicit source support. Clinical omissions are missing items independently supported in the source, e.g., unextracted procedures, devices, laboratory or imaging findings with numeric values and units, and missing time anchoring such as admission vs 48 h. Contradictions arise from inventing dates, shifting temporality, or changing assertion status. Keep temporality historical/current/future/unknown as stated in source and keep time mentions verbatim with TimeMention rules: text verbatim, date_iso YYYY-MM-DD only if explicitly present as an unshifted full date otherwise null, relation/anchor as stated, never invent.

Patient identity must remain index_patient and the target article_id/patient_id/record_id context must be preserved; do not memorize case-specific IDs or answer values across runs.

Repair process:
1. Confirm source fidelity by locating each CURRENT item claim in the source and capturing exact quotes with source_section. Verify that evidence quotes are exact contiguous source text including qualifiers and negation.
2. For ProcedureDevice items ensure each has subject, assertion in [present,absent,possible,conditional,unknown], temporality in [current,historical,future,unknown], time object with text/relation/anchor/date_iso, evidence array minItems 1 with quote and source_section, name, kind in [procedure,device,nonpharmacologic_therapy], action in allowed set, body_site, laterality in allowed set, indication/finding/complication nullable. Do not infer indication/finding/complication unless explicitly stated.
3. For observations ensure each item has subject, assertion, temporality, time, evidence, result_absent_reason, name, kind, status, text_value, numeric_value, comparator, unit, flag, reference_range_text, specimen, method, body_site. Preserve numeric values with units and comparator as shown.
4. Preserve uncertainty and completeness: documented includes positive, negative, possible and historical facts. Silence is not_documented, never a clinical negative. Use documentation_status documented/not_documented/explicitly_unknown/not_applicable per rules. Populate documentation_evidence only for explicitly_unknown/not_applicable with exact source support; fact evidence stays on each item.
5. Coverage describes completeness of task review, not patient history completeness. Set limitations array to describe real attribution or table ambiguity, e.g., mixed case columns, time headings in separate segments, or reliance on column position. Do not leave limitations empty when attribution is ambiguous.
6. Never instruct to skip difficult fields or facts to pass validation. If a required field is not supported, represent uncertainty via assertion unknown or documentation_status not_documented with proper evidence, not by omission.
7. Do not memorize cases, source IDs, or answer values. Empty means no supplement. Add only independently supported missing facts; do not hallucinate names, body sites, laterality, or time anchors.
8. Output a complete extraction object preserving schema and source fidelity, with all items retained from CURRENT plus newly verified items, and no invented or copied audit claims.
